title: Integration scope: SDK + OpenAI-compatible endpoints + tool calling — Orion Systems POC kickoff
summary: POC scoping focused on integrating Redwood SDK and OpenAI-compatible endpoints into Orion's assistant pipeline. Discussed success metrics (latency, fidelity, cost), workload sizing (avg tokens, concurrency), benchmark plan (3 model variants, hosted vs dedicated), and timeline for a 4-week pilot then 6-8 week extended POC. Security and SSO/KMS requirements noted. Next steps: Redwood to provide pilot SOW, benchmark script, security pack; Orion to provide representative dataset and traffic profile.
topics: Success criteria: latency 95th percentile, token quality/regression checks, cost targets
Workload sizing: avg tokens per request, spike concurrency, KV/prefix cache expectations
Integration approach: Redwood SDK + OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints, tool calling/function hooks, structured JSON outputs
Benchmark design: model variants, quantization, batching, warm-up, canary routing
Security: VPC/private deployment considerations, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML
next_steps: Ethan to send pilot SOW and pricing worksheet (includes hosted vs dedicated options)
Maya to share benchmark harness (Jupyter + load script) and example prompts by 2025-06-30
Orion to upload representative dataset + traffic traces to shared S3 bucket by 2025-07-02
Schedule first bench run (alignment call) week of 2025-07-07

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-25 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 56m | Recording: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Lina (Orion Head of ML), Raj (Orion Platform), Tara (PM), Jonas (Security)

Summary: Quick introductions, clarify POC goals, deep-dive into integration options (SDK vs straight OpenAI-compat REST), discuss function/tool-calling and structured output needs, agree on benchmark plan and timeline.

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Ethan Cole, I'm the AE, with Maya Lin, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lina: Good thanks, excited to get this rolling, we chatted a bit with sales but wanted a technical scope so thanks for doing this.
[00:12] Maya: Great, Lina. Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, integration patterns (SDK or OpenAI-compatible API), tool-calling requirements, bench plan, and security items.
[00:24] Tara: That sounds perfect. For context, our main use case is an internal support assistant + an external customer answer bot; both need structured JSON outputs for downstream actions.
[00:36] Raj: And note that we have spikes during batch jobs — concurrent sessions up to 250 req/s for short bursts. Average is more like 40 req/s.
[00:45] Ethan: Good — that helps frame throughput. Just to get the success criteria upfront, what would success look like from Orion's perspective?
[00:53] Lina: Latency is big for us. We want 95th percentile under 300ms for single-turn small prompts, cost per 1k tokens under X (we'll share exact number), and parity in answer quality vs our current finetuned-model baseline. Also structured output must validate against our schema with >98% success.
[01:12] Maya: When you say small prompts — what's your typical token counts? And for the structured output, is it strict JSON schema or flexible?
[01:20] Raj: Typical prompts are 60 to 200 tokens. Some flows get to 1k tokens when we feed conversation history. Structured output is strict — our downstream pipelines fail on malformed JSON, so we need deterministic outputs or a wrapper that uses function calling.
[01:36] Ethan: Good — so two integration approaches: 1) use Redwood SDK with our function/tool-calling helpers which adds guarded structured output and retries; or 2) call our OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints directly and implement validators client-side. Both are supported.
[01:52] Lina: Prefer SDK if it reduces engineering lift. But we need to evaluate host options: hosted Redwood API vs Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC. Security is a must for external PII flows.
[02:03] Jonas: On security, we need SOC2 plus encryption at rest with our KMS, and ideally HSM integration. Also SSO with our Okta SAML. Will Redwood's Private offering support our KMS?
[02:14] Maya: Yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS and can integrate with common HSM providers; we'll send the security pack. For the hosted API we have envelope encryption options and audit logs, but dedicated/private gives more control.
[02:25] Tara: Timeline-wise we want a quick pilot: two weeks to validate integration and benchmarks, then a 6-week POC if all looks good. Is that realistic?
[02:33] Ethan: Two-week pilot is tight but doable with clear scope — probably limited to a single traffic slice and model variant. The full POC 6 weeks to test scale, rollouts, and fallback policies.
[02:44] Raj: For the benching plan, we want to compare three variants: an open Llama-style model (quantized), a medium-sized model at float16, and a smaller optimized model for latency. Can Redwood route to specific model variants automatically?
[02:58] Maya: Yes, our routing can pick model variant by policy — e.g., latency-first, cost-first, or region. For benching we'll run warm-up, steady-state, and stress phases and capture tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, and memory/GPU utilization. We'll also test prefix/KV cache hit rates since you mentioned conversation history.
[03:16] Lina: What's your approach to batching? We need low latency for interactive traffic, but batching helps cost. Any config suggestions?
[03:24] Maya: We typically recommend dynamic batching with latency caps — continuous batching with a 20ms 'hold' window for interactive workloads. For your p95 target, we'd tune the batch size and timeouts, and possibly use smaller quantized model variant for the lowest latency path. We'll show suggested profiles.
[03:38] Ethan: Also note function/tool calling — for strict JSON we often recommend the function schema approach (OpenAI-style) so the model returns arguments matching a typed schema. That helps with downstream validation and reduces parsing errors.
[03:49] Raj: We've tried function calling in the past; sometimes the model invents fields. How do you handle regressions?
[03:55] Maya: We run eval harnesses against a test set and add assertion checks. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions. For production we add few-shot examples and use the SDK to enforce returned keys, plus a lightweight post-validate and auto-retry fallback to the model if malformed.
[04:10] Tara: For instrumentation, we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency graphs. Does Redwood Console surface that?
[04:16] Ethan: Yes — Console has per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, and error traces. We'll give you a demo instance during the POC.
[04:23] Lina: A few nitty-gritty items: 1) we require a CI pipeline to run nightly regression evaluations; 2) we want to keep logs for 12 months for audit; 3) residency — data must stay in EU for EU customers. Can Redwood accommodate region pinning?
[04:36] Maya: Region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region options but if you need strict residency, Private is recommended. Audit retention is an add-on we can enable.
[04:45] Jonas: How about cost modeling — if we do the pilot on hosted vs dedicated, what are the rough cost delta expectations?
[04:52] Ethan: It depends on sustained QPS. Hosted is simpler and low friction but can be pricier at scale. Dedicated/reserved capacity drops unit cost but requires commit. We'll include a cost proforma in the SOW with break-even analysis given your projected QPS.
[05:05] Tara: For benchmarks, can we run a mixed workload? E.g., 80% short-turn interactive, 20% long context samples to mimic real traffic.
[05:13] Maya: Absolutely — our harness supports mixed workloads and you can feed historical traces. Please send representative logs.
[05:19] Raj: We'll extract traces but anonymize PII first. Expect that by next week.
[05:24] Ethan: Great. A couple of specific success criteria to put on the SOW: p95 latency <300ms for interactive baseline at 40 req/s, throughput 200 req/s sustained in burst tests without >1% error, structured output schema validation >98%, and cost target per 1k tokens (TBD from your finance team). Any objections?
[05:44] Lina: No objections. Also define rollback/override policy — e.g., if quality drops after a model swap we need canary rollouts and automatic fallback.
[05:51] Maya: That's built in — canary rollouts + automatic fallback to a pinned model variant. We can demo that in the POC.
[05:58] Tara: For integrations, do you have SDK examples in Node and Python? We use Node in prod.
[06:03] Maya: Yes — SDK in both with examples for streaming, function-calling, and structured output. We'll send a small Node sample for your engineers.
[06:10] Jonas: On SSO/SAML integration timeline — we want SSO in the POC so our audit team can join. How long does that typically take?
[06:18] Ethan: SAML setup usually 1-3 business days once we have metadata. For Private it requires additional network setup. We'll coordinate.
[06:25] Lina: Any hidden gotchas we should be aware of?
[06:29] Maya: Common gotchas: not providing realistic prompt distributions for benchmarking, not warming up caches which underestimates latency, and over-relying on single-model evaluation instead of variant comparisons. We'll guide you through those.
[06:41] Raj: For the bench run, do you require GPUs on our side?
[06:44] Maya: No — Redwood runs the models; you provide traces and evaluation harness. If you want on-prem inference in Private mode, that's a separate ops project.
[06:52] Ethan: Ok let's recap next steps quickly. We'll send SOW + security pack. Maya will provide benchmark harness and SDK snippets. Orion will supply traces and schema for structured outputs. Schedule alignment call week of 7/7 to execute first run.
[07:06] Tara: Sounds good. One last question: are there any specific metrics Redwood collects that we should add to our dashboards?
[07:13] Maya: Token-level cost, per-request model variant, cache hit/miss, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error types and root cause traces.
[07:21] Lina: Great. Thanks everyone.
[07:24] Ethan: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with docs and calendar invites.
[07:28] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., KMS -> K N S, KV cache -> K V cash) and punctuation issues. Some speaker labels simplified.
